claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features repetitive minor bosses and reused enemy types such as rock monsters and giant pillar-wielding foes throughout the campaign.

citations.review_text: Good story, but too many drawn out fights with low level threats

Very nice game. 9/10. 
The starting of the game was simply epic. It set ups the mood of the game and the tone of the game. The story is also very good. We can feel the chemistry between Atreus and Kratos. The ending of the game was also very good. The last battle was epic and the emotions it carried was also good. The bond between characters felt touching.
 The game is indeed very good but it has flaws. The major flaw I felt was that in the middle of the game many time I fought with same bosses which felt repetitive. Like the one with rock, he just attacks with its big rock and legs. It was 6-7 times in the game with slightly different attribute. And the ice monster too it throw ice from middle. He also appeared 3-4 times. It makes the game a bit repetiting. If there were new and cool bosses everytime it would have been great. Plus there is a slow pace in middle of the game.
Except these things the game is good.
And I forgot to say one thing. I am the GHOST OF SPARTA.

I find this to be another example of a game deserving a middle rating on Steam were I able to give it one.

The story is great and well-executed, but it's clear that the story and cinematics were also the focus over the gameplay to the point where the gameplay took some hits, especially when compared to the original trilogy. Not to say that it was never fun, but its highs are high and its lows are low. I would complain about the combos feeling simple, but I also probably just didn't know how to use em properly half the time I will admit. Even then when comparing the game to the original trilogy, 2018 onward just feels like an oversimplification or regression, even if there is an extra layer or two under the hood.

And the bosses? Okay, let me start off by saying that the actual major bosses of the game are awesome and pretty fun to fight. The minor bosses, however, are just the same 2-3 enemy types recycled over and over and occasionally given some new abilities. Like the giant that carries a pillar as a weapon or whatever? I swear I've killed him 10 times just in the mainline story. He's not a bad enemy type by any means, I just think he's an overused one. The worst offender for me is the Soul Eater, basically a rock monster that can only be hurt when its chest opens revealing its core, and it appears in fire and ice variants. Now ordinarily a boss where you have to wait for a weak point to open up wouldn't bother me, but if you don't know or use certain skills that can melt the Soul Eater's core within seconds, this boss variant WILL turn your somewhat fast-paced hack-and-slash game into a sluggish cover shooter. Screw the Soul Eater (who also gets reused a decent amount of times) just for that. [spoiler]The worst offenders of the major bosses is probably the final boss, not because he's boring or otherwise unfun (in fact he's actually my favorite boss fight), but he uses an ability to constantly shift between fire and ice elements and you have to react to that. claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features unskippable cutscenes.

citations.review_text:
A great story game, mostly feels like watching a movie rather than playing, unskippable cutscenes make em more cinema like. 10/10

BOYYYYYY!!!

19 Hours to get it done with, onto ragnarok.......

Great level design, visuals, voice acting and animations. Game looks stunning and I am sure it has many good qualities about it. That being said, gameplay loop is boring for me. Do basic puzzle solving, walk a bit, fight for a bit, repeat with sometimes longer walking time or cutscene. Combat itself is okay but I just don't enjoy the whole gameplay loop. I tried to like it for 6+ hours and it just did not click with me. There is probably no point to forcing myself to finish it just for sake of finishing it. It's not a bad game, but it's just boring for my taste.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the camera and controls feel awkward or problematic during gameplay.

citations.review_text: Wish I could give a meh.  Very pretty movie with limited puzzles and exploration.  Absolutely abysmal combat, controls, and camera.

Really wanted to like this. The camera made that impossible. The whole thing just feels like someone that doesnt play games picked a bunch of ideas and mechanics out of a list and said this is how the game is going to function. They then proceeded to throw money and time at it trying to make it work, to make it enjoyable. its a extremely polished mess of gameplay. the story, (as much as i experienced) seems ok. the kid is irritating, and not because hes a kid or anything that normally goes along with that, but because it just doesnt make sense at times. like when the rope bridge collapses underneath him near the begining of the gamee, and hes hanging onto one of the remaining boards of the bridge.... and can not pull himself up.... like this lean , muscular, and presumably pretty badass kid, that can use a bow powerful enough to kill giant deer thing, cant pull himself up? come on.  so much forced stuff like that just feels like a slap in the face. the writing in regards to the insertion of stuff like that, is, absolutely terrible. or whoever is ultimately responsible for that. terrible.

cant begin to understand how this got game of the year.... must have been one bad year... or sony bought that title. either way, even on sale, i would say pass.

07

The gameplay is very average or even bad and a bit repetitive.
Graphics and sound are excellent
The story and script gives itself too much importance at the expense of the game. sometime less would be more in terms of lines
The over the shoulder camera is all one shot in the game, which works well at times, but it doesnt help the gameplay angle. 
Might give it another chance one day but I couldnt get into it at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat and fighting mechanics as satisfying and enjoyable.

citations.review_text:
Should've played this game many years ago. Combat's so satisfying, Kratos is soooooo hot. Voice is insanely deep! Like oh my God.

Loving how there are rarely any cuts in this game, it's like a one long one shot scene lol.

Great story and very fun fighting mechanics. graphics are great (with setting adjustments ofc)
10/10. Play with a controller if you have one.

claims.claim: Reviewers note a lack of enemy variety, particularly citing repeated encounters with trolls and standard mobs like draugr.

citations.review_text: Great game. Story is very good and keeps you interested, enemy variety is lacking both in mobbing and bosses, but valkyries make up for it :)

"The Cycle Ends Here"

I hate that it took me so long to actually sit down and fully 100% this masterpiece, but I'm so glad I did. No wonder why this game swept the game awards in 2018. From the writing, to the music, to the gameplay, the entire team at SMS was firing on all of the cylinders making this game.

The only complaints I really have from this game is the obvious ones. The enemy variety stinks. There's 12 different types of Dragur, and then every other humanoid enemy in the game follows the same archetypes but with a different element (like Ice and Poison), 90% of the bossfights are Trolls with the only unique ones being Hræzlyr, Magni and Modi, and Bauldr (who makes up three different bossfights but they're all peak so I'm not complaining. 

There is one boss you might have noticed I skipped but its because that entire segment is also hot ass. ♥♥♥♥ the Dark Elf King and all of Alfheim, it sucks and should be banished to Hel. The game would go from a 9/10 to a 10 if Alfheim didn't exist, why couldn't Odin have destroyed that tower?

But everything else about this game is peak. I highly recommend anyone who hasn't tried this game because they keep hearing bs like "it's just a walking sim" or "it's just a movie" actually give it a try because it will surprise you.

I don't know why did this game become goty. Technically it is pretty good with impressive visuals but this is all there is to it. The combat is mid since the enemies have boring patterns, bosses use the same 2-3 moves and the enemie variety is incredibly low. The level design is also mid and you spend most of the time looking around to solve puzzles which just add more meaningless gameplay time to the game. The story is also very cliche with the typical strict father/naive son relationship and you won't see any exciting plot twist or anything interesting other than some impressive cutscenes. Rdr2 really got robbed from goty if you ask me.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the areas of Niflheim and Muspelheim as involving excessive grinding and repetitive tasks for gear upgrades.

citations.review_text:
Another great game to 100%.
Pros: great graphics, good and touching story, great combats with some of them felt really epic. I saw some people complain about father and son gameplay and conversations but I found it great as a father myself. 

This game is really great and no wonder why it was goty. I recommend any fellow gamers to try it if you haven't.

Things i hate here do not impact the greatness of the game. They just make me bored sometimes and felt like time wasted. The things I hate the most are: (1) the amount of backtracking. Man, i got sick of the lake and shore of nine for how many times I have to come back there for items and new contents. And the Helheim as well. (2) The grinding at the Muspelheim and Niflheim are a bit too much, especially the Niflheim to repeatingly farm for echoes and other resources for max out gears. 

The 100% trophy of this game is straightforward, but not easy at all and many can be missed.
It's a good game but niflheim is ass

Exceeded my expectations. Very good story, it actually intrigued me well enough to consider buying the sequel. I strongly recommend you buy the game as it is a unique experience. One small nitpick is Niflheim and how repetetive it can get but other than that great game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the campaign can feel too easy on standard settings, while higher difficulties turn enemies into damage sponges.

citations.review_text:
Story and gameplay are cool, but the campaign is too easy. Then, suddenly, the later challenges become ridiculously annoying 📢.
The difficulty doesn’t come from epic battles, but from frustrating mechanics—enemies that can blind you, others that burn the ground. Instead of feeling rewarding, it just feels insufferable. Not worthy of + time outside main story.

Great game overall. The graphics are beautiful, and the story is well written. However, the main story is a bit too easy. The Valkyrie fights are where the combat truly shines and their Queen provides a real challenge.
I'd give it a solid 8/10 if Atreus weren't as annoying as he is.
Will Kratos be finally at peace once we fight another God of War ?

"God of War | 2018 | PC | Played for: 55h

I was not invested in the series (1st entry for me), nor the slasher type game and neither in the Norse mythology. By the end of the game I set my eyes on the sequel Ragnarok, and was compelled to 100% the game.

Graphics are stunning and very well optimised, artwork and sound-work are superb. Gameplay at beginning seems dull, by the end is ok. Except Valkyries bosses, on normal difficulty nothing seems to challenge, while on hard enemies are damage sponges. Petty that the light and heavy runic attacks can not be set to "random". 

Overall it is a well regarded and recommended game by most for a reason, I went sceptical into it and was hooked until the end.

Story: 8,5/10
Gameplay: 7,5/10
Graphics/Physics: 9/10
Music/Sound: 9/10
Final Score: 8,33/10

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening hours as slow or hard to push through.

citations.review_text:
I now see why this won Game of the Year back in 2018 over the likes of RDR2. It excels in its presentation to a degree essentially unmatched by any game I have every played. 

Everything looks stunning despite being 8 years old: very detailed textures but also a clear picture. Artdesign is amazing, the scale is perfect. That extends beyond the big creatures and monuments. Games often feel a little gamey in their environments, as in that they feel smaller than they should be. GoW does it perfectly. 

Sound is also very well done and detailed. It gives everything in the game its proper weight. The story reaches very high highs multiple times, music is used sparringly but that adds weight to the moments it is used. Voice acting is absolutely fantastic as well, dialogue is plentiful and never dull, and the cutscenes have excellent mocap. The transitions with the gameplay are also seemless, and the lack of loading screens really brings this world alive. 10/10 on presentation.

But it is not perfect, no game is. I found the opening hours to be very hard to push through. I had not played any God of War game, nor knew anything about it, when embarking on this journey. The narrative moves rather slowly and I was not impressed by the combat. And this is the one weakness, or rather lack of greatness, of the game: the gameplay. The exploration is good but it can drag a bit sometimes. The combat did not feel satisfying, even if it did feel crunchy. This is mostly due to the axe, it improves markedly when you get the other set of weapons, but it is a bit baffling considering the quality of all the rest and of its predecessors.

Speaking of those, I actually put this game down halfway through when Kratos' past began to be teased more and more, and played the original games starting from the original from 2005. I won't start reviewing those (except an obligatory "3 is fantastic"), but it did make me reflect even worsely on the combat in this game. It all feels much...less, less fun…

Although I felt it had a slow start if you stick with it I think the payoff is top tier.

The gameplay loop also increases in enjoyment for me as the game goes on.

claims.claim: Reviewers report experiencing graphical glitches and performance drops in open world areas or during high frame rate play on PC.

citations.review_text: 9/10 Great game Great story The combat is very difficult on lower difficulties (skill issue yes) runs bad on any system when in the open world but ran great in smaller segments.

My second playthrough (first on ps5 4 years ago). For me it's a great game for a story, but gameplay get's repetitive fast, there's also a lot of graphical glitches when you play in high fps here on pc and forced DOF. Still i think if you want an good playstation style cinematic game God of War can be clearly recommended.
